originality.rationale: Compared exact length-ceiling cardinality, period-avoidance formula, and even/odd asymptotic constants with the directly relevant symmetric fix-free coding sources (a full 2010 DCC paper and 1996 patent), with 2003 related abstract and multiple semantic database queries. Their fixed-length-sequence feasibility, average-codeword-length optimization and palindrome-constrained channel correction results do not state or imply the universal explicit ceiling formula and asymptotic constants. A 2003 backtracking paper (inspected abstract/methods) defines symmetric-child replacement in a palindrome-prefix tree, for a source-probability optimization objective rather than the displayed period-exclusion capacity; its remaining experimental sections were not fully inspected; unindexed equivalences remain acknowledged risks.
residual_risks: 2003 paper already describes symmetric-child operations on the palindrome-prefix tree, and its general tree framework could potentially be specialized to derive part of the present result.
Unindexed early reversible-code literature or patent implementations might contain equivalent terminal-tree counting.
A general mathematical all-period enumeration could imply this exact formula, but no such published specialization was found.
Remaining experimental sections of the openly accessible 2003 manuscript were not fully read; no whole-document noncoverage inference rests on the partial reading.

value.rationale: This is a naturally motivated exact source alphabet capacity problem for symmetric instantaneous codes with a maximum codeword length. The terminal-prefix/period equivalence gives an explicit all-N formula and sharp parity-dependent leading constants; for binary alphabets variable lengths improve capacity by factors tending to four and three over equal maximal length. That quantifies a substantive design tradeoff not implied by correctness or enumeration alone.
